designationHistory.name: Havasu Lake National Wildlife Refuge
designationHistory.indexText: President Franklin D. Roosevelt established the Havasu Lake National Wildlife Refuge by Executive Order 8647; in 1993 its Bill Williams River unit was designated a separate refuge.

sources.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service: Bill Williams River National Wildlife Refuge, About Us
American Presidency Project: Executive Order 8647—Establishing the Havasu Lake National Wildlife Refuge (Jan 22, 1941)

review.note: Draft gave 1977, a land purchase from The Nature Conservancy. The lands were first reserved as part of Havasu Lake NWR by EO 8647 (Jan. 22, 1941, FDR); FWS says the 6,100-acre unit became Bill Williams River NWR in 1993. EO 8647 does not name the Bill Williams delta; the link rests on the FWS refuge timeline.

designationHistory.indexOriginal: Our History January 22, 1941 – A refuge was established within Havasu Lake National Wildlife Refuge as a breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. 1977 – A large tract of land was purchased from The Nature Conservancy and incorporated into the refuge.
